newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes down before FOMC, BASF struggles.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes down before FOMC, BASF struggles.

text.p: German shares closed bourse trade down on Tuesday as dealers remained cautious ahead of a meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy setting committee, with the main market feature being drug group BASF's lawsuit woes.

The DAX-30 blue-chip index closed trade 61.12 points, 1.70 percent, lower at 3,543.33 with June DAX futures slipping to 3,527.0 as dealers said no clear market consensus had emerged on the likelihood of U.S. interest rate moves.
The IBIS DAX index of electronic trade later closed 53.06 points at 3,516.20.
Aside from worries about higher U.S. interest rates, traders said the weaker dollar was taking a toll on export-related companies, especially chemical firms.
Hoechst AG was 1.90 to 65.60 marks while Bayer fell 1.34 to 64.48 marks.
But BASF AG was hit hardest, falling 2.37 to 63.70 marks after news emerged over the weekend that it faces an $8.5 billion lawsuit in the U.S.

The lawsuit alleges BASF, U.S. unit Knoll and its Boots Pharmaceutical division concealed a university study that concluded that their thyroid drug Synthroid was no better than cheaper, generic brands to treat people suffering from hypothyroidism.
BASF has called the lawsuit unfounded and described the amount of damages sought as "grotesque".
Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG also came under pressure, falling 1.30 marks to 38.45, amid profit-taking as a tax break on trading the shares took effect.

Under German law, investors can sell shares in a company without having to pay a capital gains if they hold the shares for six months. Telekom shares later came back to close trade just eight pfennigs lower at 39.40.

Shares in Deutsche Bank AG, meanwhile, were 1.52 lower at 97.18 marks despite news first quarter profit climbed 28 percent to 1.4 billion marks and that the results confirmed the bank's forecast of higher profit for the year as a whole.
